key_insight: Swarms of off-the-shelf AI coding agents, given only a scope statement and tools, were able to produce substantial theoretical research outputs—including drafts, notes, and some formal proofs—across multiple fields with little human guidance.
engineering_relevance: The paper suggests AI agent swarms can accelerate routine theoretical work, shifting human effort from production to verification and raising new requirements for review pipelines and research governance.
method: Ran swarms of coding agents on a narrow-to-broad research scope with access to literature and computational tools.
Provided one instruction: make real, correct, useful progress and do not stop; no scientific ideas were supplied by humans.
Collected agent-generated research notes, paper-length drafts, formal proofs, and proposed experiments across six areas.
evidence_signal: The authors report that in checked outputs they found no major scientific error so far, and several results were formalized in a proof assistant, but they also note that a full review would take months.
watch_item: The main risk is verification bottlenecks: even if agent outputs are useful, correctness, novelty, and publication credit still require rigorous human review and institutional standards.
paper_title: AI Agent Swarms as Researchers: Progress, Challenges, and Open Questions
